trigger_conditions: applying np.abs to a positive NaN input such as np.nan

numerical_characteristics.dtype: float32, float64 and longdouble (test also parametrizes float16)
category_specific_evidence: Special value involved is NaN, specifically the sign bit: np.signbit(np.abs(np.nan)) returned True instead of False (issue#31421 reproducer).
Correct handling: abs of positive or negative NaN must produce a NaN with a positive sign bit (test_abs_nan_signbit).
The original bug came from the 'tmp + 0' idiom used to clear -0.0, which corrupted the sign bit of NaN (PR#31433 body).
Diff in loops_unary_fp.dispatch.c.src replaces the tmp + 0 pattern in c_abs_f32 and c_abs_f64 with npy_fabsf and npy_fabs.
PR#31433 body names LONGDOUBLE_absolute in loops.c.src as the affected function, while the diffs touch the f32/f64 dispatch code.
Affected platform reported as wasm32/Pyodide (commit message and issue link to pyodide.org 0.29.4).
Tests assert np.signbit of abs(+nan) and abs(-nan) is False for float16, float32, float64 and longdouble, and for an array [nan, -nan].
Discussion notes the float32/float64 pattern may also be affected and asks for a separate PR for those types.
reproduction_risks: Tests check only the sign bit of NaN; no passage gives values or tolerances for other special values such as -0.0, +/-inf or subnormals after the fix.
Whether fabs also preserves the -0.0 clearing behavior that the removed tmp + 0 idiom was meant to provide is not stated in the passages.
Passages disagree on which file holds the longdouble fix (PR body cites loops.c.src; diffs show loops_unary_fp.dispatch.c.src).
The reproducer prints results as observed on wasm32/Pyodide; behavior on native platforms is not stated.
The float16 coverage is requested in discussion and added in
